title: 1-2-Switch
description: 1-2-Switch is a collection of 28 compact party activities created to demonstrate the original Nintendo Switch Joy-Con controllers. Many games deliberately ask players to stop watching the display and instead react to one another's body language, timing, sounds and controller feedback. Quick Draw turns two players into Wild West duelists; Milk uses repeated motion input; Ball Count demonstrates HD Rumble by simulating objects rolling inside the controller; Safe Crack asks players to rotate a Joy-Con while feeling subtle vibration feedback; Eating Contest uses the right Joy-Con's IR Motion Camera; Samurai Training, Sword Fight, Table Tennis, Wizard, Copy Dance and other activities explore motion, timing and social interaction. The title has no story campaign, progression economy or online multiplayer. Its value comes almost entirely from short face-to-face sessions with another person.

description_short: A face-to-face party collection built around Joy-Con motion controls, HD Rumble and the IR Motion Camera, designed for two people to watch each other instead of the screen.
description_ar: لعبة حفلات لشخصين صُممت عند إطلاق Nintendo Switch لاستعراض Joy-Con. تضم 28 لعبة مصغرة تستخدم الحركة وHD Rumble وIR Motion Camera، وكثير منها يجعل اللاعبين ينظرون لبعضهما بدل الشاشة. لا تحتوي على طور قصة تقليدي أو أونلاين.
nintendoPlayModes: TV, Tabletop; Handheld Mode is not supported
nintendoNotes: Nintendo lists 1-2-Switch as a two-player-focused party game supporting TV and Tabletop modes. Handheld Mode is not supported. Some activities rely on original Joy-Con-specific hardware features, including the IR Motion Camera. No verified Full Wrap was used for 3D texture.
tagline: Put the screen aside and face your opponent in a collection of quick Joy-Con party games built around motion, HD Rumble and social reactions.
fitFor: Two-player gatherings where people want simple, immediately understandable party activities.
Players interested in the original Joy-Con’s motion, HD Rumble and IR Motion Camera features.
Families and casual groups who prefer short competitive activities rather than a long campaign.
notFitFor: Solo players; the experience is designed primarily around two people facing each other.
Players looking for Handheld Mode; Nintendo does not support handheld play for 1-2-Switch.
Players looking for a narrative campaign, online progression or deep single-player systems.

gameplayPillars.title: Face-to-Face Play
gameplayPillars.description: Many activities deliberately ask players to watch each other rather than stare at the television, making body language and reactions part of the game.

gameplayPillars.title: Joy-Con Technology
gameplayPillars.description: Motion sensing, HD Rumble and the right Joy-Con IR Motion Camera drive different minigame mechanics and demonstrations.

gameplayPillars.title: Quick Party Challenges
gameplayPillars.description: Short activities can be selected rapidly for gatherings, with simple rules designed to be understood with minimal setup.

worldSummary: 1-2-Switch does not have a traditional story world. It is structured as a collection of short party scenarios presented through live-action-style prompts and simple visual feedback. The real focus is the physical space between the two players, with the television acting as an instruction and score display rather than the center of attention.
features: A face-to-face party-game format encourages players to watch each other instead of staring at the television.
A collection of short competitive activities demonstrates motion controls, HD Rumble and other Joy-Con functions.
Designed primarily around two-player local play with simple rules that can be explained quickly to new players.
Activities include reaction tests, duels, rhythm-like challenges and physical-comedy minigames.
The presentation is intentionally social, making spectators part of the experience even when they are not holding a controller.
Nintendo’s Ver. 1.1 update added gameplay video capture compatibility on supported system software.
perfNotes: Resolution database analysis identifies 1920x1080 docked output and 1280x720 assets/handheld profile, but Nintendo officially marks Handheld Mode itself as unsupported. The game is visually simple and presented at a 60 Hz/60 FPS class rate.

devicePerformance.unavailableReason: Nintendo does not publish resolution or frame-rate figures for 1-2-Switch and no reputable technical analysis exists. Handheld play is not supported: the game is built around detached Joy-Con play in TV and Tabletop modes.

storageNotes: Nintendo currently lists 1.4 GB required space for both Switch and Switch 2 compatibility.

faq.q: Can 1-2-Switch be played in Handheld Mode?
faq.a: No. Nintendo marks Handheld Mode as unsupported; TV or Tabletop play is required.
The core experience is designed for two players.
No. It is a party-game collection made up of independent minigames rather than a narrative campaign.

verdictSummary:
Score note: 5.8/10 is a direct normalization of the current 58/100 Metacritic aggregate for the Nintendo listing; it is not a separately invented store rating.

1-2-Switch works best as a social hardware showcase: its appeal comes from direct two-person interaction and unusual Joy-Con mechanics rather than depth or a traditional campaign.
verdictPros: Strong demonstration of original Joy-Con hardware features.
Easy to introduce to casual players at gatherings.
verdictCons: Little value for players seeking a solo campaign.
Some minigames depend on original Joy-Con-specific hardware features.

setupNeeds: Two human players are recommended for the intended experience.
TV Mode or Tabletop Mode; Handheld Mode is not supported.
